items.title: Bengaluru: Police, BDA ready alternate roads to Ballari Road ahead of proposed restrictions
points: The BDA was supposed to begin work on the elevated corridor between UAS Staff Quarters and Mehkri Circle, with traffic restrictions on the airport corridor set to come into force from Friday.

items.title: Woman, critically ill son, take shelter in graveyard near Vemulawada, shifted to hospital in Sircilla
points: A 60-year-old woman and her critically ill son were forced to take shelter at a local graveyard (Vaikunta Dhamam) in Vemulawada after their house owner allegedly asked them to vacate their rented accommodation, leaving them without shelter, on Thursday.
According to sources, the woman, a native of Kistampet village in Chandurthi mandal, had been living in a rented house in the temple town with her 38-year-old son for the past couple of months.

items.title: Railways step up checks to prevent firecracker transport during festive season
points: Southern Railway’s Palakkad Division has issued an appeal to passengers to ensure a safe, incident-free festive period by refraining from carrying firecrackers, explosives, or inflammable items on trains and railway property.

Railway officials emphasised that transporting hazardous items—including fireworks, gas cylinders, petrol, diesel, kerosene, stoves, matchboxes, and lighters—poses a grave danger to passengers, staff, and infrastructure.

Even a minor spark can ignite a catastrophic fire, risking lives and property. ​Carrying or attempting to book prohibited hazardous materials as luggage or parcel freight is a severe, punishable offence under Sections 67, 164, and 165 of the Railways Act,…

Violators face imprisonment for up to three years, fines of up to ₹1,000, and full legal liability for any injury, loss, or damage caused. ​Owing to heavy passenger traffic over the holidays, security personnel have stepped up surveillance.

items.title: ‘Disco’ movie review: Stylish treatment fails to paper over the lack of substance in this generic mafia story
points: A scene from the film Disco. | Photo Credit: Special arrangement Everyday is Halloween in the ganglands of Ullas Chemban’s sophomore film Disco.
In whatever grim situation they may be caught in, the mafia men in this film somehow find the adequate time and mood to dress up in matching colourful costumes before they carry out the hit.
Going by how this keeps repeating for the entire length of Disco, its costume designer was probably working overtime.
Or, the screenwriter also pitched in, since the film borrows much of its story from typical gangster films and hopes to get away with it using its stylish treatment.
Just like Ullas Chemban’s debut work Anchakkallakokkan, Disco too is strong in its technical department, but that is not enough to save a film which banks a little too much on stylistics.
Chemban Vinod Jose, who displayed his flair as a writer in Angamaly Diaries, does not manage to do the same in Disco.

items.title: Over 6,000 pregnant women shifted to hospitals ahead of cyclones in A.P.
points: The Health and Medical Department has made extensive arrangements to safeguard pregnant women, mothers and newborn babies in view of successive cyclones affecting Andhra Pradesh.

A statement issued by the department on Friday said pregnant women nearing their expected delivery dates had been identified and shifted to hospitals in advance to avoid transportation difficulties during the cyclones.
Of the 6,166 pregnant women shifted to hospitals in areas affected by Cyclones Murasu and Arnab, 2,924 (47.42%) have delivered so far.
A total of 3,066 pregnant women were shifted to hospitals in the 13 districts affected by Cyclone Murasu.
In the 20 districts affected by Cyclone Arnab, 3,100 pregnant women were shifted to hospitals, of whom 1,219 (39.32%) have delivered.
Officials identified women whose expected delivery dates fell between October 25 and November 8 and ensured that they received the necessary medical care.
Arrangements were also made to shift 550 pregnant women scheduled to deliver at private hospitals to the respective facilities.

items.title: SEBI proposes mandatory AML certification for intermediaries’ principal officers
points: Under the proposal, principal officers will have to clear the NISM-Series-XXIV: Anti-Money Laundering and Combating the Financing of Terrorism Provisions in Securities Markets Certification Examination, conducted by the National Institute of Securities…
SEBI has proposed that existing principal officers complete the certification within six months of the issuance of the requirement.
Principal officers are responsible for overseeing AML/CFT compliance at intermediaries.
Their duties include identifying and assessing suspicious transactions, reporting them to the Financial Intelligence Unit-India (FIU-IND), maintaining records and facilitating regulatory reporting.

The certification covers provisions of the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA), SEBI’s AML/CFT framework, customer due diligence, beneficial ownership, risk-based client classification, enhanced due diligence and suspicious transaction reporting.

It also covers targeted financial sanctions, high-risk jurisdictions identified by the Financial Action Task Force (FATF), transaction monitoring and emerging money laundering risks arising from new products and technologies.
SEBI said the existing framework requires intermediaries to appoint a principal officer at the management level but does not prescribe any specific AML/CFT certification.
